assertions.name: atom_element_and_atlas_knot_do_not_share_a_markov_trace
assertions.source: Exact, symbolic in q, both in H_3, both convention D. A Markov invariant must agree on Markov-equivalent objects, so this settles the charitable reading of 'Same Markov class'.

assertions.name: proton_and_neutron_elements_are_distinguished_by_rho
assertions.source: They share an atlas knot, so Vol is shared; the p-n difference has to come from rho. It does.

description: Tests the charitable reading of the corrected 'Same Markov class' claim: do the atom H_n(q) element and its atlas knot agree on the Markov trace, the invariant rho(K) in the mass law actually is? Symbolically in q, both objects in H_3, both through convention-D machinery. They do not. Markov-equivalent objects must agree on a Markov invariant, so this measures what the category-error argument only argued.

method_guards.same_algebra: A=1 gives 3A=3 strands and (s1 s2^-1)^3 is a 3-braid; both in H_3, so no stabilisation or normalisation mismatch
method_guards.same_convention: both sides via markov_peel / markov_trace_canonical, convention D (z = q^3/(q^2+1)). Deliberately NOT via from_scratch/wenzl_y_axiomatic.py, whose z = 1/(q^1/2 + q^-1/2) is convention C -- that comparison would measure the convention, not the objects.
method_guards.symbolic: sympy in q throughout; no anchor, no dps, no float, so 'agrees to N digits' cannot arise

what_this_does_not_show.not_a_defect_in_the_framework: the division of labour is sound and was checked separately -- Vol from the atlas KNOT, rho = tr_M from the atom ELEMENT, nothing reading a topological quantity off the element. This CONFIRMS that split is real rather than redundant.
what_this_does_not_show.shared_knot_for_p_and_n_is_deliberate: both atlas to the same Borromean link on purpose: Vol is shared and the p-n difference comes from rho, which assertion 2 confirms differs.
